subject.title: Feature: configurable LLM retry with backoff on transient errors (overloaded/529)

question: What permanent public retry contract should OpenClaw expose for main LLM provider failures: provider-level retry config, agent/global retry config, both, or no new config surface?
rationale: The request adds public config/API surface and changes provider fallback timing, so automation cannot safely choose the product contract or default retry semantics.

options.title: Approve One Provider-Level Contract
options.body: Use a single provider-scoped retry block and require runtime wiring, idempotency limits, docs, schema updates, and upgrade proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Keep Retries Internal Only
options.body: Handle only narrow transient overload cases in runtime policy and decline user-configurable retry knobs to keep config surface small.

options.title: Defer To Broader Routing Work
options.body: Leave this issue open but make a broader provider routing/fallback item own retry, cooldown, and failure-class policy together.

recommendation.title: Approve One Provider-Level Contract
recommendation.body: Use a single provider-scoped retry block and require runtime wiring, idempotency limits, docs, schema updates, and upgrade proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest current-main history across provider config, provider runtime behavior, and adjacent retry/failover surfaces.
